entries.name: Webhook Tester
entries.description: Send a test request to any webhook URL and analyze the response (status, headers, body, latency), billed per call via x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://webhook-tester.api.klymax402.com/api/test with JSON body {url, method, body} where url is the target webhook to test
usage.outputShape: body.response.statusCode, body.response.statusText, body.response.headers, body.response.body, body.latencyMs, body.success; echoes body.requestBody and body.requestHeaders
quirks: Body field is 'url' = the target webhook to probe (not the API's own URL); supply 'method' and optional 'body' for the test request.
Response is sync JSON; the probed endpoint's result lives under body.response (statusCode/headers/body) and timing under body.latencyMs.
usage.guide: POST to https://webhook-tester.api.klymax402.com/api/test with a JSON body {"url": "<target webhook URL>", "method": "POST", "body": {...}} and pay $0.002 USDC via x402 on Base. The service fires the request at your target URL and returns a sync JSON analysis. Read the probed result from body.response (statusCode, statusText, headers, body) and the round-trip time from body.latencyMs; body.success indicates whether the call completed. It echoes your requestBody/requestHeaders so you can confirm what was sent.

entries.name: ToolOracle Agent Card A2A Readiness
entries.description: Deterministic automated readiness assessment of a public agent card or A2A discovery URL across eight dimensions (fetch/parse, identity, skills, protocol, auth, commercial, trust, privacy), returning a READY/WARN/NOT_READY decision, a readiness_level and a signed record digest, billed per call via x402.

job_id.description: Job id minted by the free /deal/a2a handshake (a2aj_...).

quote_id.description: x402 quote id minted by the free /deal/a2a handshake (x402q_...), bound to the assessed target.

usage.callShape: Two steps. STEP 1 (free): POST https://tooloracle.io/deal/a2a (a2a-jsonrpc) with {jsonrpc:'2.0',id:1,method:'message/send',params:{schema_version:'AgentCardReadinessTaskRequestV1',offer_id:'AgentCardReadinessOfferV1',request_id:<unique>,idempotency_key:<unique>,target_type:'agent_card_url'|'a2a_discovery_url'|'domain',target:<url/domain to assess>,accepted_terms_version:'nomos.a2a.terms.v1'}} -> mints result.payment_required.pay_with = {job_id, quote_id}. STEP 2 (paid $0.10 x402 Base): POST https://tooloracle.io/v2/agent_card_a2a_readiness_v1 with JSON body {job_id, quote_id} -> sync verdict.
usage.outputShape: Sync JSON verdict at the top level: decision (READY|WARN|NOT_READY), readiness_level (integer), status (e.g. COMPLETED_WITH_WARNINGS), job_id, credential_id (a2ard_...), record_digest (sha256:...), assessed_at. The record_digest/credential_id are the signed evidence handles for the assessment.
quirks: TWO-STEP: the paid endpoint body is only {job_id, quote_id}; the real input (the agent card / A2A URL to assess) is supplied in a prior FREE a2a-jsonrpc handshake at POST https://tooloracle.io/deal/a2a that mints the {job_id, quote_id} binding (bound to a sha256 target_digest, ~7-day expiry).

The free handshake request must be a valid AgentCardReadinessTaskRequestV1: schema_version MUST equal the literal string 'AgentCardReadinessTaskRequestV1' (not a semver), offer_id 'AgentCardReadinessOfferV1', a unique request_id and idempotency_key, a valid target_type (agent_card_url | a2a_discovery_url | domain) + target, and terms accepted via the field 'accepted_terms_version':'nomos.a2a.terms.v1' (note: 'terms_accepted'/'terms_version' are NOT the accepting field).

Result is delivered synchronously in the paid POST 200 body (no polling needed); the free status poll (POST /deal/a2a method 'tasks/get' with {job_id}) only returns status metadata (has_result, status), not the verdict.
Automated assessment only — explicitly not a certification, not regulator-approved, not an AI-Act compliance check, not a penetration test.
x402 paid $0.10 USDC on Base (asset 0x833589..., payTo 0x11f591...); confirmed on-chain (tx 0x5873ec95...). No API key / no sign-in.
usage.guide: To assess whether a public AI agent is A2A/agent-card ready: (1) FREE handshake — POST https://tooloracle.io/deal/a2a with {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"message/send","params":{"schema_version":"AgentCardReadinessTaskRequestV1","offer_id":"AgentCardReadinessOfferV1","request_id":"<unique>","idempotency_key":"<unique>","target_type":"agent_card_url","target":"https://<host>/.well-known/agent.json","accepted_terms_version":"nomos.a2a.terms.v1"}} (target_type may also be a2a_discovery_url or domain). Read result.payment_required.pay_with = {job_id, quote_id}. (2) PAID — POST https://tooloracle.io/v2/agent_card_a2a_readiness_v1 with JSON body {"job_id":"...","quote_id":"..."} and pay $0.10 USDC via x402 on Base (no API key). The 200 response is the verdict: read decision (READY/WARN/NOT_READY), readiness_level, status, and the signed evidence handles credential_id + record_digest.

entries.name: Webbersites Contrast Check
entries.description: Compute the WCAG contrast ratio between a foreground and background color (hex or rgb()), returning the exact ratio plus AA/AAA pass/fail for normal text, large text, and UI components with a plain-English verdict, billed per call via x402 on Base.

fg.description: Foreground/text color — hex (#111 or #111111) or rgb().

usage.callShape: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/a11y/contrast?fg=<color>&bg=<color> — colors are hex (#767676) or rgb(); pay $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base. Result is returned synchronously in the 200 JSON body.
usage.outputShape: Sync JSON at top level: foreground, background, contrast_ratio (number, e.g. 4.54), ratio_string ('4.54:1'), passes {normal_text:{AA,AAA}, large_text:{AA,AAA}, ui_components:{AA}} (booleans), summary (plain-English verdict), guidance (nullable), ts (ISO timestamp).
quirks: Colors are passed as URL query params fg and bg (URL-encode the '#', e.g. %23767676); both hex and rgb() are accepted. No request body — this is a GET.
Pure computation on two supplied colors (does not fetch a URL); the description notes it complements the URL-based a11y endpoint which can't do this.
The 402/200 body advertises a wallet-memory discount: passing X-Wallet / ?wallet with a wallet that spent >$0.001 in 24h halves the price to $0.0005 (optional; default is $0.001).
x402 paid $0.001 USDC on Base (asset 0x833589..., payTo 0xdd5fcEa8...); no API key / no sign-in.
usage.guide: To check WCAG color contrast: GET https://api.webbersites.com/api/a11y/contrast with query params fg and bg (foreground and background colors as hex like %23767676 or rgb()), and pay $0.001 USDC via x402 on Base (no API key). The 200 response is the verdict: read contrast_ratio and ratio_string for the numeric ratio, and passes.normal_text / passes.large_text / passes.ui_components (each AA/AAA booleans) for WCAG conformance, plus a plain-English summary.

entries.name: Agentstools Accessibility Batch Check
entries.description: Batch static WCAG 2.2 accessibility check of many UI files at once (HTML/JSX/TSX/Vue/Angular markup you supply): returns a per-file pass/caution/block verdict with rule-level findings plus a rollup of the worst verdict and totals by severity.

files.description: List of UI files to check. Each item: {filename, optional framework, markup}.

framework.description: Optional per-file framework; falls back to the top-level default.

markup.description: The raw source markup for this file.

level.description: Default WCAG level applied to every file (default AA).

framework.description: Default framework for files that do not set one.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/a11y/batch with JSON body {"files":[{"filename":..., "framework":..., "markup":...}, ...]}. `files` is the only required field; optional top-level `level` (A|AA, default AA) and `framework` (auto|html|jsx|tsx|vue|angular) set defaults for files that omit them. Result is inline in the 200. Pays $0.10 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object. Top level: object ("a11y_batch"), worst_verdict (pass|caution|block), file_count, totals.{by_severity:{block,caution}, findings}, files[], ruleset_version (e.g. 2026.07.16), wcag_version (WCAG 2.2), disclaimer. Each files[] item: filename, verdict (pass|caution|block), framework_detected, summary.{by_severity, counts.{findings, by_category}}, findings[] (each: rule_id e.g. img-alt, wcag_sc e.g. 1.1.1, wcag_level, severity, category e.g. text-alternatives, element, location e.g. "line 1", message, remediation), findings_truncated (bool), skipped_needs_render[]. Verified live: Logo.jsx -> block with img-alt finding (1.1.1); ok.html -> pass, zero findings; worst_verdict block.
quirks: STATIC analysis only — it parses the markup YOU supply; it does NOT render the page, resolve the CSS cascade, or run assistive tech, so it can miss real barriers (false negatives). Per its own disclaimer a `pass` is not proof of accessibility and it is NOT a legal compliance guarantee.
Flat per-call price ($0.10) for the whole batch regardless of how many files are in `files` — batch multiple files in one request rather than paying per file.
worst_verdict is the roll-up (worst of all files): block > caution > pass. Check per-file `verdict` for which file failed.
Findings can be truncated per file (`findings_truncated`); some elements are skipped when they need a rendered DOM (`skipped_needs_render`).
`framework` may be given per-file or as a top-level default; `auto` lets the service detect it (returned as `framework_detected`).
usage.guide: Batch-check the accessibility (WCAG 2.2) of UI source you already have. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/a11y/batch with JSON {"files":[{"filename":"Logo.jsx","framework":"jsx","markup":""}, ...]} — `files` is the only required field (each item needs at least `filename`; include `markup` for it to be checked; `framework` is auto|html|jsx|tsx|vue|angular, or set a top-level default). Optional top-level `level` (A|AA, default AA). No API key; pays a flat $0.10 USDC via x402 on Base per call for the whole batch. The 200 returns per-file verdicts (pass|caution|block) with rule-level findings (rule_id, wcag_sc, severity, element, location, message, remediation) plus a rollup (worst_verdict, file_count, totals by severity). This is deterministic STATIC markup analysis — it does not render the page, so treat results as accessibility indicators, not a compliance certification.

entries.name: Agentstools Accessibility Preflight
entries.description: Static WCAG 2.2 accessibility check of a single UI markup fragment (HTML/JSX/TSX/Vue/Angular you supply): returns a pass/caution/block verdict with per-finding WCAG criterion, element and line, plus a coverage summary.

markup.description: The UI markup fragment or component to check.

level.description: WCAG conformance level to check (default AA).

palette.description: Optional name-to-colour map for static contrast (e.g. CSS variables / theme tokens).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/a11y/preflight with JSON body {"markup":"", "framework":"jsx"}. `markup` is the only required field; optional `framework` (auto|html|jsx|tsx|vue|angular, default auto), `level` (A|AA, default AA) and `palette`/`theme` (name-to-colour map for static contrast). Result is inline in the 200. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object. Top level: object ("a11y_preflight"), verdict (pass|caution|block), findings[] (each: rule_id e.g. img-alt, wcag_sc e.g. 1.1.1, wcag_level, severity, category e.g. text-alternatives, element, location e.g. "line 1", message, remediation), findings_truncated (bool), summary.{by_severity:{block,caution}, counts:{findings, by_category}}, coverage.{framework_detected, level, rules_run, rules_total, nodes_scanned, skipped_needs_render[]}, ruleset_version (e.g. 2026.07.16), wcag_version (WCAG 2.2), disclaimer. Verified live: '' -> verdict block, one img-alt finding (WCAG 1.1.1), coverage.rules_run 14/14, framework_detected jsx.
quirks: STATIC analysis only — it parses the markup YOU supply; it does NOT render the page, resolve the full CSS cascade, or run assistive tech, so it can miss real barriers (false negatives). Per its own disclaimer a `pass` is not proof of accessibility and it is NOT a legal compliance guarantee.
Single fragment per call. To check many files in one request (and one flat fee) use the sibling Agentstools Accessibility Batch Check (POST /a11y/batch, $0.10).
verdict is the roll-up for the fragment: block > caution > pass.
Static contrast rules need a colour map — pass CSS variables / theme tokens via `palette` (or its alias `theme`) so colour-contrast rules can run.
`framework` defaults to auto-detect; the detected value is returned as coverage.framework_detected.
usage.guide: Check the accessibility (WCAG 2.2) of one UI markup fragment you already have. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/a11y/preflight with JSON {"markup":"","framework":"jsx"} — `markup` is the only required field; `framework` is auto|html|jsx|tsx|vue|angular (default auto), `level` is A|AA (default AA), and `palette`/`theme` supplies a name-to-colour map so static colour-contrast rules can run. No API key; pays a flat $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base per call. The 200 returns a fragment verdict (pass|caution|block) with rule-level findings (rule_id, wcag_sc, severity, element, location, message, remediation) plus a coverage summary (framework_detected, rules_run/rules_total, nodes_scanned). This is deterministic STATIC markup analysis — it does not render the page, so treat results as accessibility indicators, not a compliance certification. For many files at once use the batch sibling POST /a11y/batch.

entries.name: Agentstools SQL Check
entries.description: One keyless x402 call runs a safety & performance preflight on a single SQL query before you execute it — parses the statement (postgres/mysql/sqlite/bigquery/snowflake) and returns a pass/caution/block verdict with per-finding operation, severity, plain-language reason and a suggested fix.

sql.description: The query text to check. Required. JSON body field.

options.description: Optional hints, e.g. indexed_columns: list of column names to refine performance findings.

findings.description: Per-finding objects with operation, severity, plain-language reason and a suggested fix. Empty when the query is clean.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/sql/check with JSON body {"sql": "<query>", "dialect": "<postgres|mysql|sqlite|bigquery|snowflake>"} — only 'sql' is required (dialect defaults to postgres); optional 'options' object accepts hints like indexed_columns. Result is inline in the synchronous 200. Pays a flat $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.

inputExample.sql: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = 1

usage.outputShape: JSON object: object ('sqlscan_check'), dialect, verdict (pass|caution|block), findings[] (per-finding {operation, severity, reason, fix}; empty when clean), summary{block_count, caution_count, info_count}, coverage{statements_total, statements_parsed, parse_partial}, disclaimer. Verified live: dialect=postgres sql='SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = 1' -> HTTP 200, $0.02 charged, verdict 'pass', findings [], summary all 0, coverage statements_total 1 / statements_parsed 1 / parse_partial false.

outputExample.disclaimer: Automated query safety/performance indicators, not a guarantee. Destructive and correctness findings are deterministic from the query text; performance findings are heuristics — without your schema, indexes or an EXPLAIN plan they cannot confirm a slow scan, so treat caution/info as a prompt to review, not a verdict on actual runtime.

quirks: Body field is 'sql' (the query text), NOT 'query' — the discovery callHint's {"query":...} is wrong; the live 402 schema requires {"sql":...} with 'sql' the only required field.
'dialect' defaults to postgres; supported values are postgres, mysql, sqlite, bigquery, snowflake. Optional 'options' object takes hints (e.g. indexed_columns) to refine performance findings.

Destructive and correctness findings are deterministic from the query text, but performance findings are HEURISTICS — without your schema, indexes or an EXPLAIN plan they cannot confirm a slow scan; treat caution/info as a review prompt, not a runtime verdict (per the response disclaimer).
This is the single-query check; the sibling Agentstools op POST /sql/batch checks multiple queries at once, and /sql/rules just echoes the static rule catalog.
usage.guide: Preflight a SQL statement for safety and performance BEFORE running it, in one keyless paid call. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/sql/check with a JSON body {"sql": "<your query>", "dialect": "postgres"} (dialect optional, defaults to postgres; supported: postgres|mysql|sqlite|bigquery|snowflake; optional 'options.indexed_columns' refines performance findings). NOTE the field is 'sql', not 'query'. Pays a flat $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453); result is inline in the 200. Read 'verdict' (pass|caution|block) for the roll-up, iterate 'findings[]' for each {operation, severity, reason, fix}, and check 'coverage' to confirm the parser understood every statement (parse_partial=true means some statements weren't parsed). Destructive/correctness findings are deterministic; performance findings are heuristics (no schema/indexes/EXPLAIN), so treat caution/info as a review prompt. For checking many queries at once use the sibling POST /sql/batch. Verified 2026-08-07 with dialect=postgres, sql='SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = 1' -> verdict 'pass', $0.02 charged.
